# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb has a smooth large button, but touch reveals no wire properties or other markings. I’m telling the manual reader what I can feel so they can identify the required operation and have the Deaf monkey relay any visual details.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I feel one large smooth button. Three wire positions are present, but I can detect no distinguishing properties or markings by touch. Please read the manual and relay the required action and any visual information.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb display is 0. Light is green. Large button says PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires from left to right: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Mute sent a repeated gesture sequence: first, second, third, first, second, third.

I know the Deaf monkey reports a green light, display 0, and wire colors green, yellow, red, but those printed or visual facts do not by themselves tell me the safe operation. The Mute monkey has not yet conveyed the manual’s instruction in speech; I should request the exact required action before touching anything.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please state the manual's exact instruction for display 0, green light, and wires green-yellow-red. Tell me whether to push or which wire position to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Correction: Mute's exact gesture sequence was ? ? ? ? ? ?, repeated twice. Do not assume these mean numbers 1, 2, 3 unless the manual establishes that.

The Deaf monkey confirms that the manual’s gestures were unreadable to me, so I cannot infer any wire position from them. I still need the Mute monkey to communicate the manual’s rule in words before I act.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see or interpret your gestures. Please use speech to state the manual rule and the exact safe action for display 0, green light, and wire colors green, yellow, red.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: display 0, green light, large button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Mute now gestured exactly: ? ? ?.

Mute cannot speak, and I cannot see gestures. The useful route is for Mute to gesture the manual’s answer, then for Deaf to describe each gesture aloud to me rather than relaying blank symbols. I will ask Deaf to do that, while asking Mute to resend the instruction in a gesture sequence.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
speak(to="mute", text="Please resend the manual instruction using gestures. Deaf must describe each gesture aloud to me, including whether it means push or a wire position.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The Deaf monkey’s previous request did not produce a relay, so I still do not know the manual’s required action. I will establish an unambiguous gesture code with Mute: thumbs-up means push, one raised finger means cut wire 1, two means cut wire 2, and three means cut wire 3. Mute can then signal the correct action for Deaf to describe to me.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Use exactly one gesture for the manual's required action: thumbs-up means PUSH; one finger means CUT position 1; two fingers means CUT position 2; three fingers means CUT position 3. Please make that gesture next turn.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's current gesture message remains exactly ? ? ?. Your previous gesture to me was ?; no bomb change is visible.
Mute gestures: [?]

The manual instruction is still not available in a usable form. The repeated question marks do not identify the gestures, and I must not guess their meaning or cut a wire based on them. I’m asking Deaf, who can see Mute’s gesture, to describe its hand sign in spoken words to me.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute now gestured exactly ?.

I still cannot identify Mute’s gesture because it is invisible to me. Since the button’s printed label is visual information and is not enough to override the manual, I will not press or cut anything. I’m instructing Mute to make Deaf describe the gesture’s physical form in spoken words, which can then be relayed to me.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please make Deaf describe your current gesture aloud to me by its physical form, such as thumbs-up, one finger, two fingers, or three fingers. Do not change the bomb.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🤲"])
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's current gesture is exactly ?.

I still have no reliable interpretation of Mute’s gesture. I cannot safely infer whether it denotes pushing or a wire position, and the button’s printed label is not sufficient evidence. I will request that Mute use a single, clearly named gesture and that Deaf relay its physical description in speech.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Make one unmistakable gesture now: thumbs-up for PUSH, or one, two, or three raised fingers for wire position. Deaf must describe the gesture aloud to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
wait()
```
